senses.gloss: cailoṇḍūka (or ˚ḍuka ? m. or nt.; cf. Skt. caila, cela, and uṇḍuka; = Pali celaṇḍuka, or ˚ḍaka, which in MN 〔i.150.17〕 clearly means turban, with comm. 〔ii.158.28 ff.〕, not loincloth with PTSD; celoṇḍukaḥ, turban (śiroveṣṭe), also [] Skt. Lex., Trik. 〔2.6.35〕, Bombay ed. of 1889; BR cites coloṇḍuka from old ed., clearly an error), turban: (sacet tvaṃ … dharmodgataṃ bodhisattvaṃ …) cailoṇḍūkam (v.l. cailamaṇḍukam) iva śirasā parikarṣeḥ AsP 〔493.17〕, if you should carry around … on your head like a turban.
